summary: Chinese frames time with words AFTER the time phrase, and the whole phrase stands before the verb: 八点以前 ‘before eight’, 吃饭以后 ‘after eating’, 假期期间 ‘during the holidays’, 吃饭的时候 ‘while eating’, 从去年以来 ‘since last year’. ‘Until’ is 到 (after a verb: 工作到六点) or 直到 (直到十二点才回家 ‘not until twelve’); ‘since’ is 自从 … (以后 / 以来) or 从 … 以来; ‘from … to …’ is 从 … 到 …. ‘At / on / in’ a time has NO word at all: 我七点吃早饭 ‘at seven’, 星期一 ‘on Monday’, 五月 ‘in May’, 冬天 ‘in winter’ (formal writing may add 在). The clock: number + 点 (o’clock) + number + 分 (minutes), 半 for half past: 八点半, 下午三点十分. The date goes from big to small: 年 → 月 → 号 (spoken) / 日 (written): 2026年五月一号. Months are numbered: 一月 … 十二月; 三月 ‘March’ but 三个月 ‘three months’.

blocks.title: Postpositions of time — like the place words of S12
blocks.text: 桌子上 ‘on the table’ put the place word after the noun (S12); time works the same way: 八点以前, 吃饭以后, 假期期间. 以前 / 以后 even use the words for ‘front’ and ‘back’ (前面, 后面).

blocks.title: No ‘at / on / in’
blocks.text: German um fünf, am Montag, im Mai — Chinese: 五点, 星期一, 五月, just before the verb: 我五点走. (German heute also does without a preposition — Chinese does so everywhere.)

items.title: 三月 — March
points: 我三月去。 I’m going in March.

items.title: 三个月 — three months
points: 我去三个月。 I’m going for three months.

blocks.title: Where a length of time goes
blocks.text: WHEN comes before the verb (我八点工作 ‘I work at eight’); HOW LONG comes after it (我工作八个小时 ‘I work for eight hours’).

items.title: 到 — until (everyday)
points: 我们等到明天吧。 Let’s wait until tomorrow.
从早到晚 from morning till night

items.title: 直到 … 才 … — not until
points: 他直到十二点才回家。 He didn’t come home until twelve.

blocks.title: Asking
blocks.text: 现在几点？ · 今天几号？ · 你的生日是几月几号？ · 你什么时候走？— 吃饭以后。

askYourself: Is it simply WHEN (at, on, in)? → the time word alone, before the verb: 七点, 星期一, 五月.
Before / after a time or an event? → time + 以前 / 之前, event + 以后 / 之后 — the word comes after.
Until? → verb + 到 + time (工作到六点); ‘not until’ → 直到 … 才 ….
Since (up to now)? → 从 … 以来 / 自从 … (以后).
During? → noun + 期间 / 里; a clause + 的时候.
From … to …? → 从 A 到 B.
Is it HOW LONG, not when? → after the verb (工作八个小时).
A clock time? → 点 + 分 / 半; 2 o’clock = 两点. A date? → 年 → 月 → 号, big to small.
steps: Build the time phrase (time + 以前 / 以后 / 期间 …).
Put it before the verb (at the start or after the subject).
Then the verb and the rest.

traps: *我工作八点 (for ‘at eight’) → 我八点工作; 我工作八个小时 = ‘for eight hours’.
*他直到十二点不回家 → 他直到十二点才回家.
*自从明天 → 从明天起 (自从 only for the past).

quiz.why: No word for ‘at’; the time stands before the verb.
Month before day: big to small.
三月 is March; a count needs 个.
‘Not until’ = 直到 … 才 …, without 不.
以后 follows the event; 以前 means ‘before’.
How long goes after the verb; 我八点工作 is ‘I work at eight’.

notes.text: Greek puts the preposition before the time (πριν από τις οχτώ, μετά το φαγητό) and needs στις for clock times; Chinese puts 以前 / 以后 after it and needs nothing for ‘at’: 八点以前, 七点. Greek dates go small to big (1 Μαΐου 2026), Chinese big to small. πέντε και μισή ~ 五点半.
Russian до / после come before the time (до восьми, после обеда); Chinese 八点以前, 吃饭以后 come after. Russian половина шестого ‘half of the sixth’ is 5:30 = 五点半: Chinese counts from the hour just passed.

Spanish antes de / después de come before the time (antes de las ocho); Chinese 以前 / 以后 come after it (八点以前). las cinco y media ~ 五点半; Spanish dates go small to big (1 de mayo de 2026), Chinese big to small.
English before / after / until come before the time (before eight, after dinner); Chinese 以前 / 以后 come after it (八点以前, 吃饭以后). ‘At seven’, ‘on Monday’, ‘in May’ have no word in Chinese: 七点, 星期一, 五月.
French avant / après / jusqu’à come before the time (avant huit heures); Chinese puts 以前 / 以后 after it. cinq heures et demie ~ 五点半; French dates go small to big (le 1er mai 2026).
German halb sechs is 5:30 — half TO six; Chinese 五点半 is half PAST five. vor acht ~ 八点以前, with the word after the time in Chinese.

Hindi postpositions also follow the time (आठ बजे से पहले ‘before eight’, खाने के बाद ‘after eating’), as 以前 / 以后 do. Hindi has special words for 1:30 and 2:30 (डेढ़, ढाई); Chinese simply says 一点半, 两点半.

Persian qabl az / baʿd az come before the time (qabl az sāʿat-e hasht ‘before eight’); Chinese 以前 / 以后 come after it: 八点以前. Iran’s official calendar is the Solar Hijri one; Chinese dates follow the Gregorian calendar, big to small.

Marathi puts ‘before’ and ‘after’ after the time or event (जेवणानंतर ‘after eating’), as Chinese does (吃饭以后). साडेपाच ‘5:30’ ~ 五点半, but Marathi has special words for 1:30 and 2:30 (दीड, अडीच); Chinese says 一点半, 两点半.
Arabic qabla / baʿda come before the time (qabla l-thāmina ‘before eight’); Chinese 以前 / 以后 come after it: 八点以前. Arabic dates go small to big, Chinese big to small.
Hebrew lifnei / aharei come before the time (lifnei shmone ‘before eight’); Chinese puts 以前 / 以后 after it: 八点以前. Hebrew dates go small to big, Chinese big to small.
Turkish postpositions follow the time like Chinese ones: sekizden önce ~ 八点以前, yemekten sonra ~ 吃饭以后. beş buçuk ~ 五点半; but Turkish dates go small to big (1 Mayıs 2026), Chinese big to small.
Japanese puts ‘before / after’ after the time (8時前, 食事の後), writes dates big to small (2026年5月1日) and says 5時半 for 5:30 — all as in Chinese (八点以前, 2026年五月一号, 五点半).
Korean puts ‘before / after’ after the time (8시 전에, 식사 후에), writes dates big to small (2026년 5월 1일) and says 5시 반 for 5:30 — all as in Chinese.
Finnish puoli kuusi ‘half six’ is 5:30 — half TO six; Chinese 五点半 is half past five. ennen kahdeksaa ‘before eight’ puts ennen first; Chinese 八点以前 puts it after.
Hungarian fél hat ‘half six’ is 5:30; Chinese 五点半 is half past five. But Hungarian dates go big to small like Chinese ones (2026. május 1.), and postpositions follow the time (nyolc előtt ~ 八点以前).
Swahili time counts from 6 a.m.: saa moja ‘hour one’ is 7 o’clock; Chinese 七点 is 7 o’clock. kabla ya / baada ya come before the time; Chinese 以前 / 以后 come after it.
Luganda time-telling also counts the hours from 6 a.m. (essaawa emu ‘hour one’ = 7 o’clock); Chinese counts from midnight and noon: 七点 is 7 o’clock.
Vietnamese dates go small to big (ngày 1 tháng 5 năm 2026); Chinese big to small: 2026年五月一号. trước / sau come before the time (trước 8 giờ); Chinese 以前 / 以后 come after it.
Inuktitut expresses many time relations with suffixes and verb endings; Chinese uses separate words after the time or event: 八点以前, 吃饭以后.

seeAlso.note: German puts the preposition first and chooses the case: vor / nach dem Essen (dative), bis acht, seit einem Jahr (dative, with the present tense), während der Ferien (genitive), um acht, am Montag, im Mai; Chinese has postpositions (吃饭以前, 假期期间), no case, and nothing for um / am / im.
Arabic uses قَبْلَ and بَعْدَ (+ genitive), حَتَّى ‘until’, مُنْذُ ‘since’, خِلَالَ ‘during’ and فِي السَّاعَةِ الْخَامِسَةِ ‘at five’ — all before the noun; Chinese reverses the order: 吃饭以前, 五点.
Hebrew לִפְנֵי / אַחֲרֵי, עַד, מֵאָז, בְּמֶשֶׁךְ and בְּשָׁעָה חָמֵשׁ come before the time; לִפְנֵי is also ‘in front of’, just as 以前 shares 前 with 前面.
The same rule as S14: the time phrase stands before the verb.
